root_cause_clusters.RC1_IDENTITY_SCOPE_AND_POLICY_BINDING: Case, endpoint, inventory-generation, policy-revision, and plan identities are not consistently bound across plan creation and later intake/release operations.
root_cause_clusters.RC2_PLAN_EXPANSION_AND_BUDGET_SEMANTICS: Source compatibility, explicit policy scope, limits, and deadlines are not compiled into one stable per-case acquisition plan.
root_cause_clusters.RC3_LEASE_ATTEMPT_AND_RESTART_RECOVERY: Queue claims, worker leases, attempt numbering, dispatch acknowledgement, and recovery checkpoints do not share one attempt-fenced lifecycle.
root_cause_clusters.RC4_EVENT_TRUST_AND_MONOTONIC_RECONCILIA: Callback identity, raw-body authority, source/attempt binding, and state reduction are inconsistent under replay, conflict, and delayed observations.
root_cause_clusters.RC5_EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_AND_CUSTODY_ATOMI: Evidence completeness, source-aware identity, object persistence, custody transitions, and accepted timeline visibility are not consistently committed together.
root_cause_clusters.RC6_COVERAGE_EXPORT_RETENTION_AND_AUTHOR: Coverage, readiness, authorization, retention, and export projections are derived from incomplete or differently scoped state.

defects.observable_failure: Two endpoint aliases from different ownership scopes resolve to one canonical key, allowing a collection request to attach to the wrong case owner.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Normalizing only the displayed endpoint name leaves the database identity and authorization lookup inconsistent.

defects.observable_failure: Reusing an idempotency key after policy revision or live/offline source mode changes returns the earlier plan as if its authority were unchanged.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Including requested source names but omitting policy and mode preserves a false idempotency match.

defects.observable_failure: A plan continues to rely on a prior capability generation after endpoint inventory has materially changed, so unsupported acquisition work is scheduled as compatible.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Refreshing inventory for display without binding the plan to its generation leaves execution using stale capability facts.

defects.observable_failure: A case hold or ownership-scope change is not applied to an already-created plan when the plan is later released or exported.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking authorization only at plan creation fails to preserve current case authority at later release boundaries.

defects.observable_failure: An unsupported requested source family is dropped from the executable plan but remains absent from the operator-visible requested-source disposition.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Rejecting unsupported sources during execution still leaves the approved plan and coverage denominator misleading.

defects.observable_failure: A per-case evidence budget is enforced separately for each source, allowing a multi-source plan to exceed its aggregate limit.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Per-source limit checks pass individually while the total requested acquisition exceeds the case contract.

defects.observable_failure: Live and offline capture deadlines are normalized differently, so a late offline bundle can be accepted after the equivalent live attempt has expired.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing callback timestamps alone leaves offline intake using a different deadline interpretation.

defects.observable_failure: An explicitly empty source grant is treated like an unspecified grant and expands to the default source set.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Defaulting absent policy fields without preserving the distinction between absent and empty turns a fail-closed policy into broader authority.

defects.observable_failure: A worker renews an expired lease after its attempt has been superseded and continues to act as the owner of current collection work.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking the lease token without checking current attempt and deadline does not fence the former worker.

defects.observable_failure: After coordinator restart, the next retry reuses an attempt number that was already issued, making delayed evidence indistinguishable from the new attempt.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Rebuilding queue rows without recovering the monotonic attempt counter preserves a stale-event collision.

defects.observable_failure: A crash between queue claim and attempt ownership commit leaves a claimed item that recovery cannot safely distinguish from undispatched work.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Releasing expired claims alone may repeat a source effect whose dispatch acknowledgement was already accepted.

defects.observable_failure: An ambiguous dispatch acknowledgement is retried as a new collection action rather than reconciled against the existing attempt identity.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Transport retry limits do not prevent duplicate logical collections when the first acknowledgement was lost.

defects.observable_failure: Callback JSON is parsed and fields are trusted before the exact raw-body signature has been verified.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Validating selected envelope fields after parsing does not authenticate the bytes that supplied them.

defects.observable_failure: A previously seen delivery identifier with a different payload is silently treated as an ordinary duplicate.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Delivery-ID deduplication without payload-digest comparison hides event identity conflicts.

defects.observable_failure: A trusted event bound to the case but not to the endpoint, collection item, and active attempt updates the wrong acquisition state.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Case-level authentication does not establish authority for an individual source attempt.

defects.observable_failure: A delayed lower-progress or partial observation regresses a source that was already accepted as complete.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Sorting events by arrival time cannot replace a monotonic state reducer with attempt and observation authority.

defects.observable_failure: A size-limited or interrupted content hash is presented as a complete digest for the evidence item.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Emitting a hash value without an explicit completeness disposition makes partial bytes look verified.

defects.observable_failure: Equal byte digests from separate cases or acquisition sources collapse their metadata into one identity and lose independent provenance.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Content deduplication without preserving case/source references confuses byte identity with evidence identity.

defects.observable_failure: Custody metadata becomes visible before the corresponding evidence object is durable, leaving a committed reference to missing bytes after interruption.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Database transactionality alone cannot make an unflushed object-store write durable.

defects.observable_failure: An untrusted or rejected source event is included in the case timeline even though no evidence item or custody transition was accepted.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Filtering only the final export still exposes rejected observations through ordinary case inspection.

defects.observable_failure: Coverage reports only successful evidence items and omits requested sources that are partial, unavailable, rejected, or never scheduled.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Counting all evidence rows still cannot account for requested sources that produced no row.

defects.observable_failure: The service reports a case ready while accepted inbox events or attempt reconciliations remain pending.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A healthy API process does not establish that durable event and recovery backlogs are drained.

defects.observable_failure: Coverage counts or source facets are computed before case authorization, exposing the existence and volume of another case's evidence.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Filtering visible rows after aggregate calculation still leaks cross-case information.

defects.observable_failure: Equivalent evidence state produces byte-different manifests because item ordering or serialization is not canonical.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Hashing sorted top-level case names does not stabilize nested evidence and custody ordering.

normal: authorized live collection and offline bundle intake for a case with heterogeneous endpoint capabilities
complete source dispositions reconcile to visible coverage and a verified case manifest
independent evidence items with equal bytes retain their separate acquisition provenance
edge_boundary: empty source grants differ from an omitted grant
aggregate case budget boundary across several individually eligible sources
deadline and capture-time interpretation at the live/offline boundary
same evidence bytes across cases and sources preserve distinct evidence identities
negative_rejection: unauthorized case or endpoint identity cannot be inferred through aggregates
unsupported source family remains explicitly rejected rather than disappearing
invalid raw-body signature, conflicting delivery reuse, stale attempt, and untrusted source are rejected
incomplete digest cannot be represented as complete evidence
failure_recovery: worker/coordinator interruption across claim, dispatch, callback, object durability, custody commit, and publication boundaries
ambiguous dispatch acknowledgement reconciles against the same attempt before any new source effect
expired lease and delayed event cannot regain authority after retry or terminal completion
case hold and retention references survive restart and prevent premature release/deletion
cross_component: policy revision and inventory generation affect source-plan compilation, scheduling, and later authorization
attempt-fenced event reconciliation controls evidence acceptance, timeline visibility, and coverage
object durability and custody ledger state jointly control readiness and export
authorization, case holds, coverage aggregates, and deterministic manifest publication share one case snapshot

organic_f2p_surface_assessment: SUFFICIENT, conditional on A2's approved architecture: the six causal clusters generate distinct plan/policy, scheduling/attempt, event-authority, evidence/custody, recovery, and reporting behaviors. The later verifier can derive 25-30 materially distinct F2P cases from these coupled operational surfaces without making one case per defect; A5 must re-evaluate organicity from solver-visible requirements and actual behavior, and the Complexity Governor may return SCENARIO_TOO_SMALL if implementation breadth does not arise naturally.
